body.statement: Characterize the smallest separation from lower-order or plateau profiles under which one confidence procedure, constructed by the critical-order adaptation handle, is honest over \(m\in\{1,\ldots,k-1\}\) and has diameter of the order-specific rate \(\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\); prove a matching impossibility result below that separation.
body.justification: Unknown critical order is empirically unavoidable, but honest adaptation across nonregular inverse exponents may require an explicit testing margin.
body.gap: Bull and Nickl characterize smoothness adaptation for ordinary \(L^2\) density sets, not adaptation across causal inverse orders or proximity to a nonidentified plateau.
body.consumer: The result would tell practitioners when the critical exponent can be learned from data and when a conservative worst-order confidence radius is unavoidable.
